# tabiji.ai — Full LLM Context with API Response Examples

> Free AI-curated travel data API — Reddit-sourced restaurant picks, day-by-day itineraries, destination guides, destination comparisons, and unified search for 6,905 destinations. No API key required.

## What is tabiji?

tabiji.ai is a read-only static travel data API. All data is editorially curated from real traveler discussions (Reddit) and cross-validated with Google Places. Content is served as static JSON files over Cloudflare CDN. CORS is fully open — call from any origin, any client.

**Key stats:**
- 6,905 destinations (cities, regions, countries)
- 508 picks guides covering 5,864 curated places (restaurants, bars, cafes, attractions)
- 373 day-by-day travel itineraries
- 106 head-to-head destination comparisons
- 250 countries with full factual metadata
- 1 unified cross-collection search endpoint

**No API key needed. No rate limits. No authentication.**

---

## API Documentation
- [API Docs](https://tabiji.ai/api/): Full endpoint documentation with examples
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tabiji.ai/api/openapi.json): Machine-readable API specification (OpenAPI 3.1)
- [agents.json](https://tabiji.ai/.well-known/agents.json): AI agent workflow definitions (OpenAgents format)
- [agent.json](https://tabiji.ai/.well-known/agent.json): A2A Agent Card (Google A2A Protocol v1.0.0)

---

## Endpoints

### Destinations
- `GET /api/v1/destinations.json` — All 6,905 destinations (budget, season, vibes, travel styles, pitch)
- `GET /api/v1/destinations/{slug}.json` — Full details for one destination (e.g., `tokyo.json`, `paris.json`)

### Popular Picks (Restaurant & Attraction Guides)
- `GET /api/v1/picks.json` — All 508 curated "best of" guides covering 5,864 places
- `GET /api/v1/picks/{slug}.json` — Full guide with all places, editorial summaries, maps links, Reddit quotes, "what to order" tips, insider tips (e.g., `amsterdam-brunch.json`, `tokyo-ramen.json`)

### Itineraries
- `GET /api/v1/itineraries.json` — All 373 day-by-day travel itineraries
- `GET /api/v1/itineraries/{slug}.json` — Full itinerary with day-by-day activities, neighborhoods, tips, and logistics

### Comparisons
- `GET /api/v1/compare.json` — All 106 head-to-head destination comparisons
- `GET /api/v1/compare/{slug}.json` — Full comparison with categories, Reddit quotes, verdict, and FAQs (e.g., `tokyo-vs-kyoto.json`)

### Countries
- `GET /api/v1/countries.json` — All 250 countries with capitals, population, area, region, borders, currencies, languages, timezones, driving side, dial codes, flags, and maps links
- `GET /api/v1/countries/{iso2}.json` — Facts for one country by lowercase ISO code (e.g., `jp.json`, `fr.json`, `us.json`)

### Cross-Collection Search
- `GET /api/v1/search.json` — Static search index (7,923 records) for client-side search
- `GET /api/v1/search-index.json` — Full search index with tokens for fuzzy matching

**Recommended agent workflow:** Use `search.json` to find matching slugs, then fetch the full record with the appropriate detail endpoint.

---

## Data Fields

### Destination Object
Each destination includes: `slug`, `name`, `region`, `continent`, `country`, `countryCode`, `currency` (code/name/symbol), `language`, `languages`, `coordinates` (lat/lng), `photo`, `pitch`, `budget` ($–$$$$), `season`, `vibes` (array), `travelStyles` (array), `editorialSummary`, `bestFor`, `relatedPicks`, `relatedItineraries`, `relatedComparisons`, `relatedDestinations`, `sourceMeta`, `flag`, `timezone`, `drivingSide`, `dialCode`, `tapWaterSafe`, `tippingCustom`, `visaNote`

### Place Object (in Picks)
Each place includes: `name`, `position`, `cuisineTags`, `googleRating`, `reviewCount`, `priceRange`, `address`, `area`, `googleMapsUrl`, `mapsLinks`, `openingHours` (weekly grid), `openNow`, `phone`, `website`, `photo`, `verdict`, `editorialSummary`, `bestFor`, `comparison`, `whatToOrder`, `insiderTip`, `redditQuotes` (with `text`, `source`, `sourceUrl`), `sourceMeta`

### Itinerary Day Object
Each day includes: `dayLabel`, `neighborhoods`, `title`, `description`, `activities` (with `time`, `name`, `description`, `details`, `tips`)

### Comparison Object
Each comparison includes: `slug`, `title`, `destination1`, `destination2`, `categories` (with `title`, `summary`, `highlights`, `redditQuotes`, `winnerSummary`), `verdict` (with `summary`, `takeaways`, `cards`), `faqs`

### Country Object
Each country includes: `id`, `name`, `officialName`, `iso2`, `iso3`, `capital`, `population`, `area` (km²), `region`, `subregion`, `borders` (ISO3 codes), `landlocked`, `demonyms`, `startOfWeek`, `maps`, `currencies`, `languages`, `timezones`, `flag` (emoji), `flagSvg`, `flagPng`, `drivingSide`, `dialCode`, `tld`

---

The search index contains 7,923 records across all content types. Each record has:

```json
{
  "count": 7923,
  "types": {
    "destination": 6905,
    "pick": 527,
    "itinerary": 374,
    "compare": 117
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "destination:tokyo",
      "type": "destination",
      "slug": "tokyo",
      "title": "Tokyo",
      "subtitle": "Controlled chaos that somehow works perfectly. Vending machines on every corner, Michelin stars in basements.",
      "url": "https://tabiji.ai/api/v1/destinations/tokyo.json",
      "siteUrl": "https://tabiji.ai/find/?q=tokyo",
      "tags": ["Japan", "Asia", "JP", "City", "Cultural", "Family", "Nightlife", "solo", "photography"],
      "region": "Japan",
      "continent": "Asia",
      "tokens": ["Tokyo", "Japan", "Asia", "City", "Cultural", "solo", "photography"]
    },
    {
      "id": "pick:tokyo-cheap-eats",
      "type": "pick",
      "slug": "tokyo-cheap-eats",
      "title": "15 Best Cheap Eats in Tokyo",
      "subtitle": "Gyudon, udon, conveyor sushi, teishoku, standing bars & more. All under ¥1,000.",
      "url": "https://tabiji.ai/api/v1/picks/tokyo-cheap-eats.json",
      "siteUrl": "https://tabiji.ai/popular-picks/tokyo-cheap-eats/",
      "tags": ["Tokyo", "Cheap Eats", "Japan"],
      "tokens": ["tokyo", "cheap", "eats", "gyudon", "udon", "sushi"]
    },
    {
      "id": "itinerary:10-day-italy-first-time",
      "type": "itinerary",
      "slug": "10-day-italy-first-time",
      "title": "10 Day Italy Itinerary for First-Time Visitors (2026)",
      "url": "https://tabiji.ai/api/v1/itineraries/10-day-italy-first-time.json",
      "siteUrl": "https://tabiji.ai/itineraries/10-day-italy-first-time/",
      "tags": ["Italy"],
      "tokens": ["italy", "rome", "florence", "amalfi", "itinerary", "first", "time"]
    },
    {
      "id": "compare:tokyo-vs-kyoto",
      "type": "compare",
      "slug": "tokyo-vs-kyoto",
      "title": "Tokyo vs Kyoto: Which Should You Visit?",
      "url": "https://tabiji.ai/api/v1/compare/tokyo-vs-kyoto.json",
      "siteUrl": "https://tabiji.ai/compare/tokyo-vs-kyoto/",
      "tags": ["Tokyo", "Kyoto", "Japan"],
      "tokens": ["tokyo", "kyoto", "vs", "japan", "compare"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Recommended search workflow for agents:**
1. Filter `items` by `type` if needed (`destination`, `pick`, `itinerary`, `compare`)
2. Match query tokens against `tokens` or `title` fields
3. Use the matched `slug` to call the detail endpoint (e.g., `GET /api/v1/picks/{slug}.json`)

---

## Usage Notes for LLMs

- **All endpoints are GET-only.** tabiji is a read-only API — no writes, no auth, no API keys.
- **Static JSON files served via Cloudflare CDN.** Response time is typically <50ms globally.
- **Prefer detail endpoints over the index.** The index files (`picks.json`, `itineraries.json`, etc.) only contain metadata. Full content — Reddit quotes, opening hours, what to order, day-by-day activities — is in the individual slug files.
- **Cross-linking is built in.** Every destination includes `relatedPicks`, `relatedItineraries`, and `relatedComparisons` arrays so you can traverse the content graph without searching.
- **Data provenance is transparent.** Every record includes `sourceMeta` with source type, path, URL, and last verified timestamp.
- **CORS is fully open.** Call from any origin, any client, no preflight needed.

## What Makes tabiji Data Unique

Unlike generic travel APIs, tabiji data is curated from real traveler discussions (Reddit) plus editorial judgment, then cross-linked across destinations, picks, itineraries, and comparisons. Records expose provenance/freshness metadata and lighter-weight enrichment fields so agents can traverse the content graph instead of scraping pages. Reddit quotes include upvote context and source links — this is what real travelers actually say, not marketing copy.
